chapter: Hampton, Blue Note and the electric guitar
title: Blistered fingers and punishing show schedules with the Spirits
summary: He bore down so hard he got blisters in the 1930s, and the Spirits sometimes did up to seven shows a day; he always arrived tuned.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: With the electric you could kind of cut through.
See, I had to swell it out. I had blisters on my hands, man, like, . . .
Why is that?
Blisters, bearing down on that steel. You will have blisters if you bear down too hard on that steel.
Even with the electric, you mean?
That's right.
Oh, because you were playing so much.
That's right. I had to bathe my fingers
with salt and water and epsom salts and all that crap, man. I went through it.
When was that?
Years ago. In the '30s.
From playing -- when you played like with the Spirits, I suppose you did like, what, four or five shows, maybe?
Yeah. Yeah.
Six nights a week?
Some weeks we'd do seven shows a day. Midnight show. That'd come last, that midnight show, 12:00, 1:00 o'clock.
It's enough to make anybody want to get stoned.
That's right. And by that time, if you ain't stoned you wish you were.
Yeah, I've been through that myself.
I know. You ought to know it.
It gets weird. That last set.

That's right. And you can't wait until that last set is supposed to be coming on. You just, 'Oh, I want to get it over with. Get it over with.' Then the minute that man says boom, you're out there. Then some of the cats would take 20 minutes to tune up, which they don't get out there first to tune up their instruments
before they even try to go on. But I was already tuned. See, because from me hearing the music out there, during the time, you know, I'd tune up my instrument.
Uh-huh.
So when I got out there I was ready.
You were ready to go, huh?
That's right.
